joint.outcome: theorem from standard axioms with no shared-scope hypotheses: consistent with every satisfiable law set

law.label: The tetrahedral angle: any two bonds of the diamond lattice meet with cosine exactly -1/3
law.statement_en: In the diamond lattice each atom's four neighbours lie along (a/4)(±1, ±1, ±1) with an even number of minus signs. For any cube edge a > 0 and any two distinct bonds the cosine of the angle between them is exactly -1/3, so the bond angle is arccos(-1/3) ≈ 109.47°, independent of a; it lies strictly between 90° and the 120° of three coplanar rays.

hypotheses.name: tetrahedral-bond-angle#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: The bonds are the four diamond-lattice directions (a/4)(±1, ±1, ±1) with an even number of minus signs, for a cube edge a > 0. Whether a given crystal, or a four-rayed sponge spicule, has bonds or rays in these directions is an empirical question the theorem does not touch.

scope.basis: a theorem about the ideal diamond lattice; Thompson's claim that four-rayed calcareous spicules make the same angle (thompson1917-ch09-10) is a separate, pre-registered and still blocked data test
kernelChecked: Exact: for a > 0 and i ≠ j, cosAngle (bond a i) (bond a j) = -1/3 (tetrahedral_cos).
Every bond has squared length 3a²/16 (bond_sq); any two distinct bonds have dot product -a²/16 (bond_dot).
assumed: Bond directions are the diamond-lattice directions; cube edge a > 0.

sources: W. H. Bragg and W. L. Bragg, X Rays and Crystal Structure (1915), diamond; claim bragg1915-03 in claim-sources/crystals-and-form/claims.json
Data test test-data/claim-tests/crystals-and-form/bragg1915-03/result.json: COD refined diamond cell, all bond angles equal to arccos(-1/3) within numerical error
